question: What type of ventilation pressure is maintained inside an operating room to prevent outside air from entering?
explanation: Positive pressure pushes air outward when doors open, keeping airborne pathogens from entering the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why does surgical suite design incorporate progressively restricted zones?

options.A: To reduce the overall electricity consumption of the facility
options.B: To progressively lower the risk of microbial contamination
options.C: To easily monitor the movement of equipment carts
options.D: To separate surgical staff from administrative personnel

explanation: Restricting access and changing attire requirements at each zone boundary protects the patient from surgical site infections. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which surgical procedure is most typically performed in a general operating theatre?
explanation: Hernia repairs are standard general surgical procedures that do not require specialized sub-specialty infrastructure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary design requirement for equipment inside a general operating theatre?

options.A: It should remain identical for every single specialty
options.B: It must be powered exclusively by backup generators
options.C: It must be permanently bolted to the floor
options.D: It should be mobile and easily reconfigured

explanation: Because general theatres serve multiple disciplines, equipment must be portable to adapt quickly between different types of operations. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which piece of equipment is most characteristic of a cardiothoracic operating theatre?
explanation: Cardiothoracic surgeries frequently require cardiopulmonary bypass, necessitating specialized utility connections built into the room. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a theatre for a scheduled spinal fusion procedure. Which specialized operating environment is most appropriate?

options.A: A casualty theatre designed for rapid triage procedures
options.B: An orthopedic theatre with radiolucent tables and power tools
options.C: A general operating theatre with standard mobile stretchers
options.D: An ophthalmic theatre with microscopic fixation devices

explanation: Spinal fusions require orthopedic instruments and imaging tables that allow fluoroscopy, fitting the orthopedic suite profile. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is a primary structural advantage of modular operating theatres?

options.A: They feature open-air windows for natural ventilation
options.B: They require permanent masonry walls for maximum radiation shielding
options.C: They use pre-fabricated antimicrobial wall panels to reduce crevices
options.D: They rely on wooden framing for flexible room expansion

explanation: Seamless panel construction minimizes microbial growth sites and facilitates thorough cleaning and disinfection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h4)

question: How do flush-mounted service panels benefit infection control in a modular theatre?

options.A: By increasing the room temperature to kill airborne spores
options.B: By allowing patients to control their own environmental settings
options.C: By eliminating protruding joints and dust-collecting ledges
options.D: By preventing electrical surges during high-risk procedures

explanation: Flush surfaces prevent dust accumulation and make routine wipe-downs far more effective. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary surgical goal during damage control surgery in a trauma suite?

options.A: Elective tumor staging and biopsy collection
options.C: Cosmetic closure of superficial skin lacerations
options.D: Definitive anatomical reconstruction of bone fractures

explanation: Damage control prioritizes stopping bleeding and preventing infection to save a critically unstable patient before definitive repair. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why are emergency operating suites typically located in close physical proximity to the emergency department?

options.A: To share sterile instrument sterilization autoclaves easily
options.B: To allow nursing students quick access for observational study
options.C: To minimize transit time for critically unstable patients
options.D: To reduce the cost of medical gas pipeline installations

explanation: Short transit distances reduce the window of vulnerability for patients suffering from acute, life-threatening internal bleeding. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which zone within the surgical suite requires personnel to wear surgical masks and eye protection?
explanation: The restricted zone includes operating theatres where active surgeries occur, requiring masks and full surgical attire. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following areas is NOT considered part of the restricted or semi-restricted surgical suite?

options.A: The corridors connecting scrub rooms to theatres
options.B: The hospital cafeteria and main reception lobby
options.C: The sterile core holding packaged surgical supplies
options.D: The instrument processing and sterilization area

explanation: Cafeterias and main lobbies are public, unrestricted spaces outside the controlled surgical suite perimeter. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)
